landmarks.name: Ruins of Loropéni
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, these ancient stone ruins date back over a thousand years and are linked to the trans-Saharan gold trade.

wiki.extract: The ruins of Loropéni are a medieval heritage site near the town of Loropéni in southern Burkina Faso. They were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009. These ruins were the country's first World Heritage site. The site, which spans 1.113 hectares, includes an array of stone walls that comprised a medieval fortress, the best preserved of ten in the area. They date back at least a thousand years. The settlement was occupied by the Lohron or Kulango people and prospered from the trans-Saharan gold trade, reaching its height between the 14th and 17th centuries. It was abandoned in the early 19th century.

landmarks.name: Ouagadougou Grand Mosque
landmarks.writeup: A prominent religious site in the capital city, showcasing Sudano-Sahelian architectural style.

wiki.extract: Ouagadougou or Wagadugu is the capital and largest city of Burkina Faso, and the administrative, communications, cultural and economic centre of the nation. It has a population of 2,415,266 in 2019. The city's name is often shortened to Ouaga. The inhabitants are called ouagalais. The spelling of the name Ouagadougou is derived from the French orthography common in former French African colonies.

landmarks.name: Sindou Peaks
landmarks.writeup: A striking natural rock formation offering scenic views and hiking opportunities.

wiki.extract: Sindou is a town located in the province of Léraba in Burkina Faso. It is the capital of Léraba Province and the Sindou Department.

landmarks.name: National Museum of Burkina Faso
landmarks.writeup: Located in Ouagadougou, it exhibits the country's cultural heritage and traditional artifacts.

wiki.extract: The history of Burkina Faso includes the history of various kingdoms within the country, such as the Mossi kingdoms, as well as the later French colonisation of the territory and its independence as the Republic of Upper Volta in 1960.

cultural_events.name: FESPACO (Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou)
cultural_events.writeup: The largest African film festival held biennially, celebrating African cinema and culture.

wiki.extract: The Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou is a film festival in Burkina Faso, held biennially in Ouagadougou, where the organization is based. It accepts for competition only films by African filmmakers and chiefly produced in Africa. FESPACO is scheduled in March every second year, two weeks after the last Saturday of February. Its opening night is held in the Stade du 4-Août, the national stadium.

cultural_events.name: Festival International des Masques et des Arts (FESTIMA)
cultural_events.writeup: A festival dedicated to traditional masks and cultural performances from various ethnic groups.

wiki.extract: The Festival International des Masques et des Arts, or FESTIMA, is a cultural festival celebrating traditional African masks held in Dédougou, Burkina Faso. Founded to help preserve traditional cultural practices in the modern age, FESTIMA features masks and traditions from several West African countries. It is currently held biennially in even-numbered years. The most recent edition, the fifteenth, was held from February 29 to March 7, 2020, in Bankuy.

food_writeup: Burkinabé cuisine features staple foods like millet, sorghum, rice, and maize, often served with sauces made from peanuts, okra, or leafy greens. Popular dishes include tô (a millet porridge) and riz gras (a flavorful rice dish).
brief_history: Burkina Faso, formerly Upper Volta, gained independence from France in 1960. It has experienced several coups and political changes, with a history marked by efforts to promote national unity and development.

important_people.name: Thomas Sankara
important_people.description: Revolutionary leader and former president known for progressive reforms.

important_people.name: Blaise Compaoré
important_people.description: Former president who ruled for 27 years before being ousted in 2014.

current_conflicts: Burkina Faso faces ongoing security challenges due to jihadist insurgencies and inter-communal violence, particularly in the northern and eastern regions.
